project.name: Acme Stock-Reservation Service (UniBasic -> Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 feasibility POC)
project.description:
Feasibility POC for a prospective client engagement: equipment-finance ILS system, business logic in Rocket UniData/UniBasic, target Java 17+.
Translates reserve-stock.pick, an AUTHORED representative sample (NOT sourced from a public repository) written to exercise the READU...LOCKED / RELEASE record-locking idiom, which the small public calibration corpus (github.com/zelenko/pick) does not contain. From a signed unibasic spec (spec/v1, schemaId=unibasic, targetStack=java-spring):
- The three-way OPEN/READU outcome (found-and-locked / locked-by- another-user / not-found) becomes a sealed LockOutcome result type rather than nulls or booleans, so every caller must handle all three branches explicitly. - Explicit RELEASE-on-every-exit-path is replaced by normal Java transaction-boundary semantics (the port's save() implies commit; throwing a domain exception implies rollback) rather than a manually-tracked release call.
Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj only). UniData/UniVerse have no free/scriptable runtime, so source-execution equivalence is NOT claimed here — same honest posture as every other archetype in this platform. A genuine client engagement must validate the exact locking semantics against the client's real UniData source before this ships.
